targets.productDescription:
The Book of Later Han (Houhanshu, 後漢書) tells the story of the Eastern Han dynasty, from Liu Xiu's restoration of Han rule after Wang Mang's collapse to the court struggles, frontier wars, factional purges, and regional breakdown that eventually led toward the Three Kingdoms period. It is the third work in the Twenty-Four Histories, continuing the tradition established by Sima Qian's Records of the Grand Historian and Ban Gu's Book of Han.

Fan Ye, writing during the Liu Song dynasty, compiled the imperial annals and biographies. The version transmitted today also incorporates the treatises from Sima Biao's continuation of Han history, giving the work its familiar shape as a comprehensive official history. Houhanshu preserves major accounts of the Guangwu restoration, the powerful consort clans and eunuch factions of the later Han court, the campaigns and diplomacy of the Western Regions, and the scholars, officials, generals, and critics who shaped the dynasty's political life.

This English edition of Houhanshu is part of a new translation effort by translator and editor Garrett M. Petersen to create a comprehensive translation of all 24 official dynastic histories, as well as the Draft History of Qing (Qingshigao, 清史稿) and the Comprehensive Mirror in Aid of Governance (Zizhi Tongjian, 資治通鑑). The effort is AI-assisted, with significant human editorial oversight and tuning. New technology has made it feasible to translate the nearly 40 million combined Chinese characters of these works into clear, readable English.
